content.text:
Spike, then replace: move callisto add's interactive prompts from dialoguer to inquire. Trail #487. Worktree wp-add-inquire, branched from origin/wp-interactive-cli-compare (PR #638). Why: crates/callisto-cli/src/tty.rs grew a hand-written Ctrl-C state machine (static AtomicU8 with u8 constants and a _ arm, Once + process::exit from the ctrlc thread, saved termios via rustix) because dialoguer's console backend raises SIGINT itself; four review rounds kept finding races in it. inquire (MIT) reads Ctrl-C/Esc as key events through crossterm, returns InquireError::OperationInterrupted / OperationCanceled, and restores the terminal on drop. Step 1: check inquire's latest stable version is at least two weeks old, its license passes deny.toml (just audit), and that it provides what the wizard needs: MultiSelect with default selections and page size, Select, Text with validation, Confirm, Editor using VISUAL/EDITOR, and a render config for a consistent theme. Step 2: rewrite the add wizard on inquire, keeping its behaviour and messages (changed packages first and preselected, review screen, multi-line summary via editor, next-step line, json mode never prompts). Map OperationInterrupted and OperationCanceled to one CliError variant that main turns into exit 130 with 'Cancelled, nothing written.' (Drop-based cleanup, no process::exit in library code). Delete the ctrlc and rustix runtime deps, the statics, Once and the termios code if no longer needed; the editor child still goes through runner::child_command's environment filtering (use inquire's editor with a custom command, or keep our edit() helper without signal state). Keep init on dialoguer for now unless switching it is trivial. Step 3: the existing pty tests (Enter-through, Esc, Ctrl-C at select and at text input, json refusal, empty EDITOR, editor abort) must pass unchanged in intent; run them. Report: lines removed vs added, deps removed/added, test results, and anything inquire can't do. If inquire can't meet the wizard's needs, stop after step 1 and report. Push to a new branch and open a draft PR that states it supersedes #638's tty.rs design. cargo test -p callisto-cli, just lint, just audit. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be fast and lean; GitHub CI runs the full suite, so don't duplicate it.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Local checks: `cargo test -p <touched crate>` and `just lint` (clippy) for the crates you touched; `just doc-check` if docs changed. Do not run local `just ci` or a fresh reviewer unless the lead asks; let GitHub CI do the full run.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.
